top.title: ‘Rare,’ ‘That Does Not Deserve a Double Bang’: Fans Debate Mike Breen’s Call as Mikal Bridges Sinks Buzzer-Beater to Beat Trail Blazers
top.description: Mikal Bridges © Imagn Mikal Bridges came to the rescue for the New York Knicks when he drained a buzzer-beating 3 to give his team a 97-96 win over the Portland Trail Blazers. On the local commentary team, play-by-play announcer Mike Breen made a rare “Bang, bang” call to punctuate Bridges’ clutch shot. As a testament to Breen’s iconic commentary, the “double bang” call became a subject of dispute among fans on social media. Some fans weren’t in favor of Breen using this special call on this occasion, while others were simply hyped. “That does not deserve a double bang,” one fan tweeted . Breen, a recipient of the Basketball Hall of Fame’s Curt Gowdy Media Award, has made the “Bang, bang” call on only a few occasions. These include game-winners from Steph Curry and Luka Doncic. Bridges’ heroics in the clutch sent Madison Square Garden into a frenzy, but earlier in the game, it didn’t appear that a buzzer-beater would be necessary. The Knicks led by as many as 26 points, but Damian Lillard and Donovan Clingan spearheaded a Blazers comeback. Two free throws by Deni Avdija with less than four seconds left gave the Blazers their only lead of the night. Portland appeared to have stolen a game from the Knicks on their home floor. But on the final possession, Josh Hart found his old Villanova teammate near the left wing. Bridges drove, took a step back to free himself of Toumani Camara’s defense, and made the shot as time expired. “We Do It for Those Guys”: Mikal Bridges Gives a Shoutout to Former Knicks Players After Sinking Game-Winner at MSG Mikal Bridges’ clutch shot came on Homecoming Night at the Garden. In attendance were former Knicks players like Walt “Clyde” Frazier, Earl “The Pearl” Monroe, Nate Robinson, and J.R. Smith. In his post-game interview, Bridges gave a shoutout to these Knicks of yesteryear. “We do it for those guys. Happy we could do this on their night.” Saturday also happened to be Monroe’s 82nd birthday. For the Basketball Hall of Famer, a birthday present came in the form of a game-winning shot. An NFL team viewed you as its franchise QB, but to get you had to fork over one of the most popular figures in its history. Michael Elston Phipps disappeared from Cleveland 50 years ago and for the most part was never heard from again. He did surface on camera with a gray head of hair in 2022, accompanied by his former college teammate Don Kiepert. “This is Purdue” interviewer Kate Young asked about his Browns days. “Have you ever been booed?” Phipps said. top.description: Good morning! Go for nothing but net today. Coming up: 🏈 Big Ten bananas 🏆 Current’s championship ⚽ Poch’s first United match Madness: Big Ten day of chaos It always happens like this: At the moment when we least expect it, college football reaches out and shakes us with a Saturday that stuns the season. On a day with just one ranked-versus-ranked matchup (No. 1 Georgia 34, No. 21 South Carolina 6), we got nine hours of national chaos. The most shocking results occurred in the Big Ten. The day began with perhaps the sport’s most jaw-dropping moment of all: Matt Rhule’s Nebraska beat a ranked opponent in the form of No. 14 Ohio State, 31-28. That snapped a 31-game ranked losing streak that dated back to 2016, and came on the tail of some maddeningly close losses to prestigious opponents (Indiana and Oregon) earlier this season. The Buckeyes will need to beat Michigan to finish 8-4, but even that would mean a disaster of a year under Ryan Day. Then came two different upsets, both in overtime: Michigan 18, No. 4 UCLA 16. This one took three overtimes, as the unbeaten Bruins lost both the game and their quarterback, Ty Dieffenbach (who himself was already a backup). That Michigan would win was far from a shock, given its elite defense. But the unit gave up a late tying drive before knocking Dieffenbach out of the game during the first play of OT. Third-stringer Madden Iamaleava (the sophomore brother of injured starter Nico) was way out of his depth as the game continued: UCLA did not get a first down after Dieffenbach’s injury. Washington 27, No. 8 Indiana 24. The Huskies blocked two Indiana field goals, including the tying attempt in overtime. The Hoosiers have been breaking down for weeks but kept winning close games … until now. Additional injuries on the offensive line, at linebacker and potentially at wideout will make everything even harder. top.description: The New York Jets (2-8) will face the Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) in Week 11 at SoFi Stadium. The Jets will be looking to snap a five game losing streak and also break a pathetic streak of no touchdowns from the offense in nine quarters. The Chargers finally got their first win of the season this past Monday night, defeating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20. For both teams, it’s also a bit of a dilemma on whether winning this game is a bad thing. A win for either team means they will drop in the draft order, which will frustrate fans of both teams looking for a high draft pick in the first round. For the Jets, a win may be an easier pill to swallow as they have three first-round picks in the 2027 draft, including the Colts pick acquired last year in the Sauce Gardner trade. With Bailey lining up on the left side, he’ll match up against Burke, who is massive at 6’9", 315 lbs. Burke was selected in the fourth round of the 2026 draft and has been pretty steady on the right side of the offensive line. He does struggles with pass blocking, where he ranks at the bottom of the league. He's allowed 22 pressures and a sack on the season. top.title: One fan claims Texas senator-elect James Talarico got booed during Longhorns appearance
top.description: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images James Talarico will take office this January, but before that, he made an appearance at a Texas Longhorns game, where the reception was reportedly less than stellar. Talarico won the senatorial race in Texas against Ken Paxton, becoming the first Democratic senator-elect in the state since 1993. However, even with his resounding victory in the midterm elections, Talarico may not have received the positive response many would have expected when he made an appearance at the Texas Longhorns game. Did James Talarico get booed at Texas Longhorns game? A video of James Talarico appearing and waving at the crowd during a Texas Longhorns game went viral on social media. However, there were many in the comments on the video who suggested that the video had been layered with music to drown out the sound of the senator-elect being booed. One fan wrote: “Had to add music because he was booed!” However, another fan quickly clarified that this wasn’t the case, noting: “I was there, and this is a lie. He received overwhelming cheers, particularly from “Bo French’s student section“. He is a Longhorn grad who just beat the brakes off Paxton.” A third fan who was in attendance as well made the same point: “Our whole section was cheering. Don’t know what these other people were watching.” However, a simple search of game footage showed that Talarico didn’t receive any major negative response when he was shown on the big screen at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday. Given the recent negative reception that Senator Ted Cruz received when attending a Longhorns game, the narrative that Talarico also got booed may have a political element to it. top.description: LSU head coach Lane Kiffin. © IMAGN via Reuters Connect LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin finds himself in the middle of a disappointing season. LSU lost Saturday’s game against the Tennessee Volunteers, marking the program’s fifth loss of the season, with four coming against ranked opponents. Kiffin also became the first LSU coach since Curley Hallman to lose four or more SEC games in his debut season. Hallman finished 3-4 in conference play during his first season in 1991. Before Hallman, Gaynell Tinsley had suffered five SEC defeats in his debut season in 1948. Fans shared their thoughts on LSU’s latest loss under Kiffin. “Karma for Kiffin right now,” one fan said. “They’re not gonna make him give back any money, so it panned out perfectly for him,” one fan wrote. “Ahhh, that’s how you ruin a program with name RECOGNITION 😂 hire Lane Kiffin,” one fan noted. “Should have stayed at Ole Miss,” one fan commented. “Saw this coming from a mile away,” one fan added. After the latest loss against No. 9 Tennessee, Kiffin’s record against AP Top-10 opponents dropped to 6-20. His road record against those teams is even worse at 1-10, including eight consecutive defeats. He is also winless in four games against top-10 opponents this season. What’s Left For Lane Kiffin’s LSU After Tennessee Exposed Sam Leavitt & Co. Saturday’s loss was a result of LSU’s ineffective offense, led by quarterback Sam Leavitt. In the 27-13 loss, the Tigers allowed eight sacks and 13 tackles for loss. Leavitt completed 27 of 39 passes for 222 yards, and LSU managed only 43 rushing yards. According to CBS Sports , the Tigers committed three turnovers and 16 penalties, their highest penalty total in a game since 1995. LSU has one regular-season game remaining against Arkansas on Nov. 28. top.title: Verstappen a constant amid chaos as he says Russell is 'so far below my level'
top.description: Max Verstappen has won three of the four Las Vegas Grands Prix [Press Association] Warning: This article contains offensive language Max Verstappen was a constant amid the chaos at a remarkable Las Vegas Grand Prix. He was the star figure in a race that had 34 overtaking moves for the lead in 50 laps and 352 overall, in which the biggest advantage the leader ever had was 1.5 seconds, and in which there were five cars fighting nose to tail for the lead to the final lap, and for much of the race many more than that. Even better for Verstappen, George Russell made a critical mistake 24 hours after he had revived his long-standing, on-off spat with the Dutchman. Russell, who had been Verstappen's main threat from the start of the race, locked up his brakes and speared into the barrier trying to pass Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second place behind Verstappen with two laps to go. Verstappen said: "He speaks a lot next to the track, and it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that, you know? "And today, karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening. I was, like, "Fantastic, my day is only getting better." "And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete." Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable' Verstappen felt motivated to make these remarks because of what Russell had said the day before. After an on-track altercation in practice, the pair had had an exchange of views in the stewards' room. Then, after Verstappen took pole from Russell - after fastest man Antonelli's five-place penalty was taken into account - the Briton took a pop at the Dutchman. "I am not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else," Russell said. "Somebody has got to stand up to that guy." In the paddock, a number of people felt that Verstappen was probably not the right "guy" to pick a fight with. Even though Russell was fighting with Verstappen throughout the race, the nature of their drives was different. Russell would pass the Red Bull on the straight. Then Verstappen would reclaim the lead in more extreme fashion, on the outside of the fast kink leading on to the pit straight, or on the outside again at the long Turn Three. Hardly anyone else even tried these moves, let alone pulled them off. Verstappen made them look routine. After his error, Russell managed to extricate himself from the crash barrier, but he had turned a certain podium finish into a ninth place. It was the perfect encapsulation of a season in which almost nothing has gone right. For Verstappen, it was almost too good to be true. top.title: Pontypool front row inducted into hall of fame
top.description: Graham Price, Bobby Windsor and Charlie Faulkner won a total of 88 Wales caps between them [Getty Images] Individually they were wonderfully talented but together, they were fearsome. The Pontypool front row of Tony 'Charlie' Faulkner, Bobby Windsor and Graham Price would become the stuff of rugby legend. The trio were the bulwark of a ferocious club side, the all-conquering Wales team of the Seventies and the British and Irish Lions. Now, 43 years after Price retired, the last of the trio to do so, they have become the 187th, 188th and 189th inductees of World Rugby's Hall of Fame. "Rugby is often referred to as the ultimate team sport," said John Eales, chairman of the Hall of Fame panel. "And yet, within every team there are often units that, through their dominance, style and standards, transcend generations. "The Pontypool front row were one such unit. Playing in many great Pontypool, Welsh and British and Irish Lions teams, Graham Price, Bobby Windsor and Charlie Faulkner stood out as individuals but excelled as a unit." In January 1975, against France, the trio became the first entire front row from the same club to start a Wales game. They would go on to play a total of 19 times for Wales as a unit, losing just four of those games. As a unit they twice enjoyed Five Nations Grand Slam success for Wales in 1976 and 1978, either side of a Lions tour to New Zealand in 1977. So well known - and feared - the trio were referred to as the 'Viet Gwent' in a song called Up and Under, Here We Go by popular Welsh entertainer Max Boyce. Price played a record 12 successive Test for the Lions. Faulkner died in February 2023, aged 81, though his nephew Lyndon was appointed chairman of the Welsh Rugby Union in November.

top.title: Takeaways from Maryland football’s 35-21 loss to No. 18 USC
top.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 21: Quarterback Malik Washington #7 of the Maryland Terrapins rolls out to pass as defensive tackles Tomuhini "Tom Tom" Topui Jr. #52 and Jaimeon Winfield #45 chase in pursuit during the fourth quarter at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on November 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Kevin Terrell/Getty Images) | Getty Images Maryland football brought a two-game winning streak to the West Coast for a matchup with No. 18 USC. Despite that fact, it was a major surprise when the Terps entered halftime up a point on the hosts. But on a day where several stunning upsets happened across the Big Ten, the Terps couldn’t hang onto any Hollywood magic of their own. The Trojans stormed back and scored 22 unanswered points to open the second half, as Maryland repeatedly neutralized its own hopes at making a comeback. Here are three takeaways from the Terps’ road finale. Defense can’t catch a break Maryland’s defense had made a habit of bending without breaking under interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim’s tutelage. The Terps continued to get gashed in man coverage following the leadership change, but twice against Wisconsin and four times against Purdue, Maryland stopped its opponents within the final 25 yards, forcing a field goal. It initially appeared that trend would continue in California, but as the Terps stayed on the field longer and longer, the defense visibly wore down. By the end of the game, Maryland couldn’t keep up with the West Coast offense. Out of the first 24 minutes of the game, Maryland possessed the ball for just 6:15. However, that appeared to be more of an issue of the defense being caught asleep early. top.title: Sam Bennett, Linemates Put on a Show for the Panthers. Good Thing, Eh
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect SUNRISE — Sam Bennett got his second hat trick of the season for the Florida Panthers in Saturday’s win against the Buffalo Sabres. The story, however, was the play of Bennett’s line. At least according to Paul Maurice . “They don’t get a lot of notice because of some of the other names,” Maurice said, “but that’s a win on one line tonight, and they deserve all the credit for it.” Hard to argue. Bennett scored Florida’s first three goals in Florida’s eventual 4-3 win against the Sabres — but it was Sandis Vilmanis who netted the game-winner late in the third. Bennett’s shot from the slot appeared to hit Vilmanis with the puck dropping to the ice. Vilmanis turned on it and beat Alex Lyon giving the Bennett/Vilmanis/ Eetu Luostarinen line a hand in all four goals. The trio combined for four goals and three assists. Not too shabby. “Sometimes you feel like you have a little extra jump in your step,” Bennett said. “I thought our whole line was feeling really good tonight. We were moving well. It was fun to play with them. Lots of speed and direct plays and yeah, I think we found some chemistry there.’’ Maurice was not as thrilled with the rest of his team’s play saying the only redeeming thing to come from the win — aside from the victory itself — was the play of Bennett’s line and goalie Jacob Markstrom . Florida struggled to handle the puck, their lackluster clearing attempts leading to Buffalo’s second goal which gave the Sabres a 2-1 lead. A lot of stuff Maurice did not like will be addressed today when the team practices at the arena as part of the team’s annual PanthersFest. “We have an opportunity to be a better hockey team against Ottawa,’’ Maurice said. “And we will be a better hockey team.” Still, a win is a win. And, the team made a little bit of history. Or at least Bennett did. With his second hat trick of the season, Bennett gave Florida its sixth such game in 24 games. The last NHL team to have six hat tricks before Game 25 was the Pittsburgh Penguins in 1991-92. The Panthers have, at times, had trouble scoring. Other times, the goals have come in bunches. “It definitely makes it fun,’’ Bennett said. “Obviously, hat tricks aren’t the goal. The goal is to get wins, but obviously, it you know feels good and have a bunch of different guys who got them. top.title: Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud
top.description: A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds. Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an application under the US government’s Coronavirus Food Assistance Program. He was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. at a federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska. The Nigerian will also serve one year of supervised release after his imprisonment and face deportation from the United States, the statement said. Prosecutors said Arinze, who was living outside the US at the time, sent an email to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska, on September 28, 2020, seeking financial assistance under the programme. The email, titled “CFAP Forms,” contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program, known as CFAP2, alongside an Automated Clearing House payment form. Both documents were submitted in the name of a dairy farmer identified in court records as Victim 1 and contained the farmer’s Social Security number. The US authorities said Arinze knowingly used the identification number belonging to the farmer without authorisation to validate the application. He was later brought to the United States to face prosecution over the offence. The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was established by the US Department of Agriculture during the COVID-19 pandemic to support agricultural producers affected by declining sales and rising marketing costs. The initiative was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service. Its first phase ran from May 26 to September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, opened from September 21 to December 11 of the same year. The programme allowed applicants to self-certify their eligibility without submitting evidence of pandemic-related business losses. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case. top.title: Goals, goals, goals: Die Roten Bullen charge onwards and upwards
top.description: Goals, goals, goals: Die Roten Bullen charge onwards and upwards Registering seven victories and not a single stalemate, RB Leipzig coach Martin Demichelis has refined a successful formula by combining abundant energy with merciless finishing. Even at the rear, numbers stack up well when you exclude six conceded at the Allianz Arena – Luis Díaz was quite simply unplayable that day and fully deserved his hat-trick. So, take that domestic drubbing out of the equation and the defence has been breached eight times. Borussia Dortmund, boasting one of the best backlines in Europe, have conceded a league-best seven. Sitting in fourth position, Leipzig remain within three points of the current leaders in black and yellow. Some might say that the most controversial club in German football has gone under the radar up until now, at least to those looking casually from the outside in. Unbeaten at the Red Bull Arena with an impressive 15-point haul from five outings, the stadium has become an impenetrable fortress. Of course, the biggest challenges on home soil await: one a week before Christmas and the other in February. If we look back at the summer’s revolving door, a seemingly irreplaceable Yan Diomande left to ply his trade under José Mourinho. Xaver Schlager, troublesome and tenacious on any pitch, joined Nottingham Forest. Neil El Aynaoui and Rocco Reitz have plugged that Austrian gap, while Brajan Gruda – currently on loan from Brighton but joining permanently for approximately €30 million next year – has filled the void left by a certain Ivorian. Antonio Nusa quite rightly continues to attract interest from elsewhere, yet the club’s ability to identify talent and provide the right platform alleviates concerns on that front ahead of the January transfer window. With the mid-week Champions League visit of Lens approaching, internal focus now understandably shifts as much-needed points are on offer. One win and three defeats – the latter coming against heavyweight opposition – leave them in 29th place, although it has to be said that Europe is not where Demichelis and his men will be judged.

nigeria.title: Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud
nigeria.description: A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds. Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an application under the US government’s Coronavirus Food Assistance Program. He was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. at a federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska. The Nigerian will also serve one year of supervised release after his imprisonment and face deportation from the United States, the statement said. Prosecutors said Arinze, who was living outside the US at the time, sent an email to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska, on September 28, 2020, seeking financial assistance under the programme. The email, titled “CFAP Forms,” contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program, known as CFAP2, alongside an Automated Clearing House payment form. Both documents were submitted in the name of a dairy farmer identified in court records as Victim 1 and contained the farmer’s Social Security number. The US authorities said Arinze knowingly used the identification number belonging to the farmer without authorisation to validate the application. He was later brought to the United States to face prosecution over the offence. The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was established by the US Department of Agriculture during the COVID-19 pandemic to support agricultural producers affected by declining sales and rising marketing costs. The initiative was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service. Its first phase ran from May 26 to September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, opened from September 21 to December 11 of the same year. The programme allowed applicants to self-certify their eligibility without submitting evidence of pandemic-related business losses. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case. nigeria.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: NEMA deploys technical team as death toll rises
nigeria.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The National Emergency Management Agency ,NEMA, said it has deployed a technical team to Bayelsa State to reinforce ongoing search and rescue operations following a boat accident that has now claimed 24 lives and still counting in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities. The boat was conveying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony when it capsized. NEMA in a statement signed by Manzo Ezeki of NEMA Press Unit, said 24 survivors had been rescued, while 24 bodies had been recovered as of Saturday, bringing the number of confirmed fatalities to 24. Search and rescue operations were still ongoing at the time of the announcement. The agency disclosed that 19 of the survivors were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others, who sustained varying degrees of injuries, were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for medical treatment. The deployment of the technical team followed the earlier activation of NEMA’s South-South Zonal Directorate and the mobilisation of an emergency response team from its Port Harcourt Operations Office to the accident scene. The agency said it is coordinating the rescue operation alongside the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local divers and other emergency responders. Governor Douye Diri visited the scene of the accident, where he expressed grief over the loss of lives and condoled with the families of the victims. He also commended the emergency agencies, security operatives, local divers and other responders for their intervention and continued efforts to locate possible survivors despite the difficult riverine terrain. NEMA expressed sympathy with the Bayelsa State Government and the families affected by the tragedy, pledging to sustain its collaboration with relevant authorities to coordinate the rescue operation. Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. entertainment.description: Sade Adu in the Performer category and Fela Kuti in the Early Influence category, both inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Class of 2026. Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu were officially inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame during a star-studded ceremony at the Peacock Theatre. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist. From left, Made Kuti, Femi Kuti, Yeni Kuti, and Seun Kuti in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Speaking on the milestone, the family reflected on how remarkable it is to see Fela receive both the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in the very same year. Meanwhile, Sade Adu —born Helen Folasade Adu in Ibadan—was inducted in th e Performer category as the frontwoman of her acclaimed British band Sade , alongside longtime bandmates Stuart Matthewman , Paul Spencer Denman , and Andrew Hale . sports.title: Pontypool front row inducted into hall of fame
sports.description: Graham Price, Bobby Windsor and Charlie Faulkner won a total of 88 Wales caps between them [Getty Images] Individually they were wonderfully talented but together, they were fearsome. The Pontypool front row of Tony 'Charlie' Faulkner, Bobby Windsor and Graham Price would become the stuff of rugby legend. The trio were the bulwark of a ferocious club side, the all-conquering Wales team of the Seventies and the British and Irish Lions. Now, 43 years after Price retired, the last of the trio to do so, they have become the 187th, 188th and 189th inductees of World Rugby's Hall of Fame. "Rugby is often referred to as the ultimate team sport," said John Eales, chairman of the Hall of Fame panel. "And yet, within every team there are often units that, through their dominance, style and standards, transcend generations. "The Pontypool front row were one such unit. Playing in many great Pontypool, Welsh and British and Irish Lions teams, Graham Price, Bobby Windsor and Charlie Faulkner stood out as individuals but excelled as a unit." In January 1975, against France, the trio became the first entire front row from the same club to start a Wales game. They would go on to play a total of 19 times for Wales as a unit, losing just four of those games. As a unit they twice enjoyed Five Nations Grand Slam success for Wales in 1976 and 1978, either side of a Lions tour to New Zealand in 1977. So well known - and feared - the trio were referred to as the 'Viet Gwent' in a song called Up and Under, Here We Go by popular Welsh entertainer Max Boyce. Price played a record 12 successive Test for the Lions. Faulkner died in February 2023, aged 81, though his nephew Lyndon was appointed chairman of the Welsh Rugby Union in November.

sports.title: Takeaways from Maryland football’s 35-21 loss to No. 18 USC
sports.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 21: Quarterback Malik Washington #7 of the Maryland Terrapins rolls out to pass as defensive tackles Tomuhini "Tom Tom" Topui Jr. #52 and Jaimeon Winfield #45 chase in pursuit during the fourth quarter at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on November 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Kevin Terrell/Getty Images) | Getty Images Maryland football brought a two-game winning streak to the West Coast for a matchup with No. 18 USC. Despite that fact, it was a major surprise when the Terps entered halftime up a point on the hosts. But on a day where several stunning upsets happened across the Big Ten, the Terps couldn’t hang onto any Hollywood magic of their own. The Trojans stormed back and scored 22 unanswered points to open the second half, as Maryland repeatedly neutralized its own hopes at making a comeback. Here are three takeaways from the Terps’ road finale. Defense can’t catch a break Maryland’s defense had made a habit of bending without breaking under interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim’s tutelage. The Terps continued to get gashed in man coverage following the leadership change, but twice against Wisconsin and four times against Purdue, Maryland stopped its opponents within the final 25 yards, forcing a field goal. It initially appeared that trend would continue in California, but as the Terps stayed on the field longer and longer, the defense visibly wore down. By the end of the game, Maryland couldn’t keep up with the West Coast offense. Out of the first 24 minutes of the game, Maryland possessed the ball for just 6:15. However, that appeared to be more of an issue of the defense being caught asleep early. On USC’s first drive, running back King Miller averaged 7.3 yards a carry, while quarterback Jayden Maiava found receivers in space outside the numbers for big gains. Despite that, a false start 11 yards from paydirt forced the hosts into a field goal. “I didn’t feel like the defense had the same energy that I saw the last two games,” Abdul-Rahim said. After the break, Maryland’s offense had a chance to extend the lead. But after Sean O’Haire missed a 53-yard field goal, it sputtered. Maryland’s first second-half drive, which culminated in the miss, lasted 4:40. The Terps’ next three drives lasted a combined 3:07 and went a cumulative 23 yards. After each of those, USC scored. Quarterback Malik Washington’s interceptions to end two of those drives were backbreaking. Maryland gifted its opponents generous field position, but just as critically, it denied its own defense a chance to breathe. By the end of that stretch, the defense was visibly a half-step slower. The Trojans faced less and less resistance as the points piled up. “That’s part of the game of football,” safety Lavain Scruggs said. “Physically, yeah, we probably was a little beat down, but at the end of the day, we still have to play defense to stop them from scoring. sports.title: Sam Bennett, Linemates Put on a Show for the Panthers. Good Thing, Eh
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect SUNRISE — Sam Bennett got his second hat trick of the season for the Florida Panthers in Saturday’s win against the Buffalo Sabres. The story, however, was the play of Bennett’s line. At least according to Paul Maurice . “They don’t get a lot of notice because of some of the other names,” Maurice said, “but that’s a win on one line tonight, and they deserve all the credit for it.” Hard to argue. Bennett scored Florida’s first three goals in Florida’s eventual 4-3 win against the Sabres — but it was Sandis Vilmanis who netted the game-winner late in the third. Bennett’s shot from the slot appeared to hit Vilmanis with the puck dropping to the ice. Vilmanis turned on it and beat Alex Lyon giving the Bennett/Vilmanis/ Eetu Luostarinen line a hand in all four goals. The trio combined for four goals and three assists. Not too shabby. “Sometimes you feel like you have a little extra jump in your step,” Bennett said. “I thought our whole line was feeling really good tonight. We were moving well. It was fun to play with them. Lots of speed and direct plays and yeah, I think we found some chemistry there.’’ Maurice was not as thrilled with the rest of his team’s play saying the only redeeming thing to come from the win — aside from the victory itself — was the play of Bennett’s line and goalie Jacob Markstrom . Florida struggled to handle the puck, their lackluster clearing attempts leading to Buffalo’s second goal which gave the Sabres a 2-1 lead. A lot of stuff Maurice did not like will be addressed today when the team practices at the arena as part of the team’s annual PanthersFest. “We have an opportunity to be a better hockey team against Ottawa,’’ Maurice said. “And we will be a better hockey team.” Still, a win is a win. And, the team made a little bit of history. Or at least Bennett did. With his second hat trick of the season, Bennett gave Florida its sixth such game in 24 games. The last NHL team to have six hat tricks before Game 25 was the Pittsburgh Penguins in 1991-92. The Panthers have, at times, had trouble scoring. Other times, the goals have come in bunches. “It definitely makes it fun,’’ Bennett said. “Obviously, hat tricks aren’t the goal. The goal is to get wins, but obviously, it you know feels good and have a bunch of different guys who got them. So yeah, we can we can definitely keep them coming.’’ ON DECK: GAME No. 25 OTTAWA SENATORS at FLORIDA PANTHERS When: Wednesday, 7 p.m. Where: Amerant Bank Arena, Sunrise Local TV: Scripps Sports — WSFL 39 (Miami/FTL); WHDT 9 (WPB); LAFF 36.3 (SWFla) Streaming: Panthers+ , ESPN+ Radio: WQAM; WBZT 1230-AM (Palm Beach); WCTH 100.3-FM (Florida Keys); SiriusXM. So, take that domestic drubbing out of the equation and the defence has been breached eight times. Borussia Dortmund, boasting one of the best backlines in Europe, have conceded a league-best seven. Sitting in fourth position, Leipzig remain within three points of the current leaders in black and yellow. Some might say that the most controversial club in German football has gone under the radar up until now, at least to those looking casually from the outside in. Unbeaten at the Red Bull Arena with an impressive 15-point haul from five outings, the stadium has become an impenetrable fortress. Of course, the biggest challenges on home soil await: one a week before Christmas and the other in February. If we look back at the summer’s revolving door, a seemingly irreplaceable Yan Diomande left to ply his trade under José Mourinho. Xaver Schlager, troublesome and tenacious on any pitch, joined Nottingham Forest. Neil El Aynaoui and Rocco Reitz have plugged that Austrian gap, while Brajan Gruda – currently on loan from Brighton but joining permanently for approximately €30 million next year – has filled the void left by a certain Ivorian. Antonio Nusa quite rightly continues to attract interest from elsewhere, yet the club’s ability to identify talent and provide the right platform alleviates concerns on that front ahead of the January transfer window. With the mid-week Champions League visit of Lens approaching, internal focus now understandably shifts as much-needed points are on offer. One win and three defeats – the latter coming against heavyweight opposition – leave them in 29th place, although it has to be said that Europe is not where Demichelis and his men will be judged.

technology.title: Come for the science, stay for the big iron: Supercomputer admin on why he loves the job
technology.description: Web hosting might seem like an unlikely on-ramp to supercomputer administration, but it set Mark O'Shea on his way to running some of Australia's most powerful machines. O'Shea is team leader for supercomputing operations and senior supercomputing systems administrator at Australia's Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre . Pawsey is home to Setonix, an HPE Cray EX supercomputer with more than 200,000 AMD EPYC CPU cores and hundreds of AMD Instinct MI250X accelerators. Its GPU partition ranks 87th in the November TOP500 and 37th in the Green500 , which measures computational performance per watt. "Working in web hosting wasn't much different to what I was doing a few years later with supercomputers," O'Shea tells The Register . "Datacenters are essentially several thousand computers, as are supercomputers. "So, we essentially had the same problems," he says, especially as regards cooling and power management. There's no single formal route into supercomputer administration in Australia, O'Shea says. He picked up the necessary skills over time. Andrew Underwood, Dell's chief technology officer for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence across the Asia-Pacific, Japan, and China, says that lack of formal training means some supercomputer admins start in academia. He's observed that many HPC admins emerge from the sciences, catching the computing bug during their studies. A biologist working with a massive genomics database, for example, might discover a taste for running the systems behind it. "The biologist might decide they want to be someone working in IT helping other biologists transform their industry," Underwood says . "One of the things I really admire about people who work in the supercomputing field is they take it so seriously," Underwood adds. "It's almost a passion, a hobby, more so than it is a job." "They want to play that real supporting and foundational role of assisting and engaging with scientists to help them use the technology to solve the problems the world faces." O'Shea agrees, noting that many people who get into supercomputer admin are PhD graduates who stick around their universities after they graduate. Some of them gravitate toward running the departmental computers and then wind up in supercomputing. "There are many roles around universities allowing people to be introduced to [supercomputer administration] while still doing enterprise-style or more departmental admin for researchers and system administration," O'Shea says. Regardless of how a supercomputer admin gets their gig, both O'Shea and Underwood say the supersysadmin community is tight knit – which may not always be a good thing. "As an industry in supercomputing, we need to be open to people from diverse backgrounds," Underwood says, "and we need to build these frameworks like the Student Cluster Competition, conferences like eResearch and the SC Conference, where students can get educated and systems admins get exposed to continual training." science.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. Hotels, roads, buses and archaeological sites will all face extraordinary pressure. My biggest concern isn't necessarily the number of people watching the eclipse, but the logistical chaos it will create. Let's take Mallorca as an example for the 2026 eclipse. Authorities there had a plan for its west coast, the prime viewing region. Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate . What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image — and many similar images — is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. The featured image was taken by the robotic Juno spacecraft in 2018 during its 14th low pass over Jupiter . science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

science.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest big-screen adventure
science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

NASA’s SBIR/STTR program provides support for entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses to advance and commercialize technologies that can advance the agency’s missions. Working with the program, a company’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies.
